package.title: Retatrutide and Type 2 Diabetes: What the Phase 2 Trial Showed

social.instagram_caption:
Retatrutide in type 2 diabetes: what an early Phase 2 trial showed (investigational, not approved as of Oct 2026).

Retatrutide is an investigational weekly injection that acts on GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon receptors — the same GLP-1 receptor semaglutide targets, plus more.

In a Phase 2 trial of 281 adults with type 2 diabetes (Lancet, 2023):
→ HbA1c dropped an average of 2.02 percentage points at 24 weeks on retatrutide 12 mg (stepped up from a lower dose), vs −0.01 on placebo and −1.41 on dulaglutide 1.5 mg
→ Average body weight lost at 36 weeks was 16.9% on retatrutide 12 mg, vs 3.0% on placebo and 2.0% on dulaglutide 1.5 mg
→ Most common side effects were gastrointestinal — nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting, constipation — mostly mild to moderate

Retatrutide is NOT FDA-approved as of October 2026. A planned filing isn't approval. Please never buy it online — ask your doctor about approved options or clinical trials instead.

Save this before your next appointment, and share it with someone asking about retatrutide.

#Retatrutide #Type2Diabetes #GLP1 #MetabolicHealth #DiabetesResearch #ClinicalTrial #InforMed #HbA1c #DiabetesCare

Not personal advice. Don't stop or change your current medicines on your own. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

sources.title: Retatrutide, a GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon receptor agonist, for people with type 2 diabetes: a randomised, double-blind, placebo and active-controlled, parallel-group, phase 2 trial conducted in the USA

factcheck.summary:
This carousel passes. Every trial number matches the published Phase 2 trial (Rosenstock et al., Lancet 2023). That covers the 281 participants, placebo / dulaglutide 1.5 mg / several retatrutide doses, ages 18–75, HbA1c 7.0–10.5%, BMI 25–50, and diet and exercise alone or with stable metformin. The HbA1c change at 24 weeks was −2.02 on retatrutide 12 mg (stepped up), −1.41 on dulaglutide and −0.01 on placebo. Weight change at 36 weeks was 16.94% on retatrutide 12 mg, 2.02% on dulaglutide and 3.00% on placebo. Side effects were mostly mild to moderate and gastrointestinal.

The status line is also accurate. As of October 2026 retatrutide is not FDA-approved and has not been filed; Lilly is reportedly aiming to file in Q1 2027.

The safety lines are all there: "Not personal advice", the prescriber line, don't stop or change medicines alone, never buy online, and ask about approved options or trials. The title and hook pay off.

I couldn't open the Lancet page directly (it returns 403 to automated tools). I checked the numbers through the full-text PDF mirror and published summaries instead.

The issues below are minor polish only, and none of them blocks shipping.

issues.claim: Placebo 3.0% vs Dulaglutide 1.5 mg 2.0% vs Retatrutide 12 mg 16.9%
issues.problem: The numbers are right. But a viewer with the sound off may be confused or misled when placebo loses more weight than the active comparator, and nothing on the slide explains it.
issues.fix: Change the body to: "Average % of body weight lost at 36 weeks, Phase 2, adults with type 2 diabetes; retatrutide 12 mg stepped up from a lower dose. Differences between placebo and dulaglutide were small (Lancet, 2023). Common side effects: nausea, diarrhoea."

issues.problem: The filing plan isn't credited to anyone or dated, which our attribution rules require.
issues.fix: Change the body to: "Fact: it's investigational. As of Oct 2026 it isn't FDA-approved, and Lilly's planned filing isn't approval. Never buy it online. Ask about approved options or trials."

issues.claim: Average HbA1c change at 24 weeks, top dose
issues.problem: "Top dose" alone doesn't name the drug, so a viewer with the sound off can't tell whose dose it is.
issues.fix: Change the headline to: "Average HbA1c change at 24 weeks, retatrutide 12 mg"

issues.claim: retatrutide 12 mg (stepped up) cut HbA1c by 2.02 percentage points at 24 weeks vs 1.41 on dulaglutide. Weight loss at 36 weeks: 16.9% vs 3.0% placebo, 2.0% dulaglutide.
